rules.problem: Type and trigger are right and every red-box criterion is listed. Two problems: (1) the abuse/self-harm cue is reduced to Cigarette burn, dropping shaped burns, repeated/unexplained burns and other unexplained injuries, and it sits in a task named 'urgent features' though it comes from the non-urgent section; (2) footnote 1 defines when 'shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) but nothing on the page's shock definition is encoded beyond the nurse recording Shock as a finding, so pulse >= 100, RR > 30, restlessness and weakness are never checked for. Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention to the patient with burn/s and any of'; (and Burn (or ...)) matches the box; partial thickness is correctly and-ed with the > 10% bands and full thickness stands alone. Minor: the 10-19% band admits exactly 10% where the page says > 10%, and 'Over 70 percent body burnt' is redundant. Footnote 1's 'shock likely' criteria are not modelled as a probable Shock diagnosis, so shock only counts if the nurse records it directly (SBP < 80 is covered separately).

rules.rule: (missing) Diagnose probable shock in patient with burns
rules.problem: Footnote 1 says 'If SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely' - a 'likely' diagnosis on the page with no probable rule. The brief treats every 'X likely' as a probable diagnosis; the priority rule could then reference (active_condition Shock). Whether the footnote means all-of or any-of is a question for a clinician.

summary: All 76 claims resolve to real SNOMED concepts and the red-box logic (Urgent, and/or structure, partial-thickness-and->10%, probable inhalation injury via active_condition) is faithful to the page. The most consequential problem is that the abuse and self-harm 'consider' rules fire only on cigarette burns while the page also names shaped burns, repeated/unexplained burns and other unexplained injuries, and that item is filed under the 'urgent features' task. Secondary: footnote 1's 'shock likely' criteria (pulse >= 100, RR > 30, restlessness, weakness) have no probable Shock rule; the 10-19% TBSA band admits exactly 10% where the page says > 10%; 'Over 70 percent body burnt' is redundant; and Peripheral oxygen saturation is a closer concept for SpO2 than Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen if VHA's vitals allow it.
